class_id: a precedence rule ranks an input type that no reader ever produces, so the rule is dead
feature: any priority, override or precedence table (source ranks, document-type ranks, config layers) whose entries name an input the pipeline stores but never parses
symptom: a precedence table says type X outranks type Y, and X is fetched and stored, so every part of the chain looks present. But the reader that turns X into field values does not exist or does not list X, so X never produces a value and Y always wins. Nothing fails: X rows exist with a terminal status such as NOT_EXTRACTABLE, the table is valid, and every test of the table passes because it feeds values directly. Universal shape: a ranking over producers is only as live as the set of producers that actually emit; a rank for a silent producer is documentation, not behaviour.
